 2027 Medicare Part B Premium Rates
 November 17, 2026 My Federal Retirement 
 The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services ( CMS ) announced the 2027 Medicare premiums and deductibles on November 17, 2026. The standard Medicare Part B premium will be $209.40 a month in 2027, an increase of $6.50 from $202.90 in 2026. The annual Part B deductible rises $9, to $292. CMS attributes the increases mainly to projected growth in healthcare spending.
 The final premium came in slightly below the $209.50 estimated in the projected Medicare premium increase for 2027 , and the deductible matched the $292 projection.

 The 2027 increase is 3.2 percent, or about $78 over a full year. That is far smaller than the roughly 10 percent jump in 2026. Beneficiaries who pay the standard premium will see the new amount beginning in January 2027.
 Part B covers physician services, outpatient hospital care, certain home health services, durable medical equipment and other medical services not covered by Part A. Individuals who keep Part B coverage of immunosuppressive drugs after a kidney transplant pay a standard premium of $125.70 in 2027.
 How Part B Premiums Are Paid
 Most retirees have the Part B premium deducted from their Social Security benefit, so the larger premium reduces the net deposit. The COLA Watch page covers the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA). Federal annuitants who are not yet receiving Social Security are billed directly. Details are in how Medicare Part B beneficiaries can pay their monthly premiums .
 Ad 
 Turn 65, and your FEHB decisions get harder — not easier 
 Whether to keep FEHB, add Medicare Part B, or do both isn’t a simple yes-or-no — and the wrong call can mean paying for coverage you don’t need. This workshop lays it out, plus everything else you need to know. Get the details at a free FedImpact Workshop near you .
 A hold-harmless provision limits the increase for some people whose premium is deducted from Social Security. It does not protect people who pay an income-related surcharge or who are newly enrolled. The Social Security Administration ( SSA ) explains how premiums are set and collected.
 2027 Part B Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amounts
 Higher-income beneficiaries pay an Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount (IRMAA) on top of the standard premium. CMS says the surcharge affects roughly 9 percent of people with Part B. It is based on modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) from the tax return filed two years earlier, so 2027 premiums reflect 2025 income. The first threshold is $112,000 for individual filers and $224,000 for joint filers. Beneficiaries who believe the income used is outdated can learn how to appeal Medicare Part B and Part D high monthly premiums .

 2027 Medicare Part A Premium, Deductible and Coinsurance
 Part A covers inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facilities, hospice, inpatient rehabilitation and some home health care. About 99 percent of beneficiaries pay no Part A premium because they have at least 40 quarters of Medicare-covered employment. Beneficiaries with 30 to 39 quarters pay $328 a month in 2027, up $17 from $311. Those with fewer than 30 quarters pay the full premium of $597 a month, up $32 from $565.

 Medicare Open Enrollment
 Medicare open enrollment runs October 15 through December 7. It is the window to compare Original Medicare with Medicare Advantage and to choose a Part D plan. Federal retirees can review Medicare Advantage vs. Original Medicare for federal retirees , along with the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) open season dates and FEHB premium rates . Anyone new to Medicare should read about understanding Medicare enrollment periods, deadlines and penalties . Official plan and coverage information is at Medicare.gov .
